newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swap-July gas oil under sell pressure.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swap-July gas oil under sell pressure.

text.p: Singapore front month gas oil swaps came under renewed sell pressure at midday on Wednesday amid fears of a prompt physical overhang leading to a widening of the July/August time spread, traders said.
"July gas oil is under pressure because there are a lot of aggressive physical offers for prompt cargoes," a trader said.
July swaps were last quoted at $20.50/$20.70 per barrel down from Tuesday's $20.90/$21.00, brokers said. July traded earlier in the day at $20.68 and $20.70, they said.
August was quoted unchanged from Tuesday at $21.60/$21.80 with deals done in the morning at $21.70 and $21.65, brokers said.
As a result, the July/August spread widened to value at around 85-90 cents, brokers said. The spread traded on Tuesday at 75 cents, they said.
Traders said the fresh sell pressure on July swaps was due to the sustained aggressive physical offers late Tuesday which has yet to draw out any buying interest.
On Tuesday, July gas oil was offered to a low of $20.80 per barrel, down 50 cents from Tuesday's lowest offered level.
"Gas oil was offered below $21.00 for the first time in over a year but still no one was interested in buying. The market is quite despressed," a trader said.
Gas oil prices are at their lowest level since October 1995 and traders said the near term outlook is not promising due to the lack of fresh regional demand.
Traders are hoping the production cuts would help alleviate the current high stock situation.
The jet/gas oil regrade was steady with August and September quoted at $1.75/$1.85 with an early day August trade seen at $1.75, brokers said. August regrade traded on Tuesday at $1.80.
Fuel oil was also steady following earlier fresh physical support from a local trader who on Monday bought two 20,000-tonne cargoes at $99.00 per tonne.
August and September swaps were quoted at $98.75/$99.50 per tonne, brokers said.
